title: Ring starvation and inflight imbalance scratchpad
body:
Goal:
Quick, messy notes from the last two weeks of microbenchmarks exploring a pattern we've started calling 'ring starvation' — observable tail-latency spikes when TP/PP mixes run on topologies with unbalanced NVLink rings and intermittent PCIe staging. Trying to capture hypotheses, traces, and short experiments to iterate on mitigations.

Summary of the phenomenon (observed):
- Setup: 8-GPU nodes, combination of PP (3-way) + TP (2-way) shards across GPUs, context lengths 1K-4K, batch concurrency 4-16.
- Under steady QPS the 95/99 latencies are OK, but occasional tails (10–30x median) appear correlated with:
  - small interleaved packet bursts (many small token requests hitting different replica sets),
  - NCCL collective stalls that appear as one or two GPUs not progressing for 5–20ms then draining,
  - host staging traffic (PCIe reads) overlapping with cross-node transfers.
- Term coined: 'ring starvation' — during a collective ring step a GPU's send buffer is starved of tokens because its incoming queue is delayed by a previous, unrelated small transfer, causing the whole ring to stall until a retry/poll completes.

Key traces & artifacts:
- perf+Trace logs attached in linked PR; sample timestamps show a ~12ms gap between recv call entry and completion on GPU-3 during a cross-node allreduce.
- NIC counters show burst of small RDMA packets interleaved with larger payloads (coalescing disabled on NIC for these runs).
- NCCL trace (instrumented) shows pattern: allreduce-enter -> progress spin -> fallback to host staging -> host-transfer -> resume -> collectives finish.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Micro-packet interleaving causes NIC/rdma engine context switches and increases per-packet overhead; ring algorithm depends on low variance for fairness and gets skewed.
2) Small-message lots (e.g., many concurrent short KV-cache replays) cause a head-of-line blocking at the host DMA queue, delaying the larger, latency-sensitive reductions.
3) NCCL's scheduling of ring hops doesn't account for asymmetric link latencies; a slightly slower hop repeatedly becomes the bottleneck and other hops back up (amplifies under mixed TP/PP).
4) PCIe read amplification when GPUs rely on host-staging (fallback path) produces bursts of DMA completion interrupts which preempt NIC progress threads.

Microbench experiments run so far:
- micro-1: homogeneous TP-only baseline (2-way) 
  - median: 18ms, p99: 36ms, tails negligible
- micro-2: TP+PP mix w/o KV activity (no cache replays)
  - median: 22ms, p99: 45ms
- micro-3: TP+PP with synthetic small-packet background (64B messages at 2k qps)
  - median: 23ms, p99: 82ms, p999: 210ms (clear tailing)
- micro-4: disable NIC coalescing 
  - tail worse (p99 moved to 130ms), suggests coalescing helps in this topology but not a full fix
- micro-5: enable per-NCCL pacing injection (artificial sleep between hops)
  - median +5–8ms, tail reduced by ~40%
- micro-6: aggregated small messages into 1kB batches at the producer side
  - tail improvement (p99 ~ 55ms), but increases median slightly due to batching delay

Instrumentation notes (how we observed):
- Added lightweight hooks in nccl progress to log spin counts and fallback events (sparse sampling).
- Captured GPU-side kernel timestamps with nvtx ranges; correlated to NIC RX/TX timestamps (RDMA counters) from the node's telemetry system.
- Kernel-side counters: queue-depth on host DMA, NIC intr count, per-GPU progress loops. Useful fields: spin_count_before_fallback, fallback_taken, host_dma_wait_ms.

Immediate short experiments to run (next 48–72h):
- E1: Run micro-3 but with RDMA coalescing tuned (increase aggregation on NIC) to see if coalescing consistently helps across topologies.
- E2: Run micro-3 with driver-level interrupt affinity forcing NIC progress threads onto isolated cores (reduce host preemption).
- E3: Try NCCL backoff parameter tweaks (reduce spin max, longer backoff) to avoid tight spin loops that starve host.
- E4: Instrument small-message path to batch at source (inference runtime) for a subset of requests and measure impact on user-visible latency.

Longer-term mitigations to prototype:
- Inference runtime: small-message aggregator that coalesces reply/control messages into 1–2kB bursts within 1–2ms window. Tradeoff: adds controlled jitter but reduces NIC churn.
- NCCL-level: adaptive hop-skip — if a hop shows repeated micro-delays, reorder ring traversal to avoid the noisy link for a short window (requires topology hints).
- Host/DMA: increase scatter-gather batching on DMA or tune PCIe completion coalescing.
- Scheduler: request-aware placement: colocate TP shards that communicate frequently on NVLink islands and place PP partitions to minimize cross-node ring traversal.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the root cause primarily NIC-level or DMA/PCIe scheduling? The interplay looks strong — need single-variable isolations (NIC coalescing vs. PCIe coalescing).
- How much of this is specific to our NCCL version/build? We need to reproduce with upstream 2.x builds and our tuned tree.
- Cost/benefit of batching small messages inside the runtime vs. waiting for kernel/driver-level fixes.

Notes to self (implementation details):
- For E2 use node image 'perf-2024-11-01' (already has perf tools and custom driver).
- Add an experiment label to metrics: rt.expt=ring-starve-202411. Put an alert to SRE if p99 > 200ms for more than 30m during the run.
- Save raw NCCL traces to s3://redwood-perf/rt/ring-starve/ for offline analysis; compress with zstd before upload.

Slack threads / prior art references:
- See thread #eng-llm-perf from Oct 29: discussion about small-packet RDMA effects.
- Paper-ish: "RDMA microbursts and tail latency in datacenters" (internal copy linked in PR).
- Related internal docs: small-packet-interleaving-tail-latency-study.json (we should not duplicate but this is complementary; our angle is focused on mixed TP/PP + ring behavior).

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: run E1 and E3, collect traces, post results to PR. (due 2024-11-09)
- Marcus: prototype small-message aggregator in runtime (PoC) and run micro-6. (due 2024-11-12)
- Elena: reproduce failing run on upstream NCCL and capture any diffs; validate with different driver versions. (due 2024-11-10)

If we can consistently reduce tails with a runtime aggregator + small NCCL pacing tweak, that gives a deployable mitigation we can roll out without waiting on NIC/driver patches. If not, escalate to infra team to investigate NIC firmware/driver interrupts and DMA coalescing knobs.
